title: Recursive extension of a comparison family
statement: For an exact augmented complex N' with differentials d and augmentation η, a complex F with free terms and differentials δ, and a₀ : F 0 ⟶ N' 0 satisfying δ 0 ≫ a₀ ≫ η = 0, there exists a family α i : F i ⟶ N' i with α 0 = a₀ and α (i+1) ≫ d i = δ i ≫ α i for every i.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00LS, proof of lemma-compare-resolutions (1), lines 17525--17535

proof.text: Free source terms are projective. Use Mathlib CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Exact.liftFromProjective at the exact augmented short complex to lift δ 0 ≫ a₀; its required zero composite is precisely the added hypothesis. The companion liftFromProjective_comp theorem gives the first compatibility equation.

For each i retain a pair (a,b) of adjacent comparison maps with b ≫ d i = δ i ≫ a. Then (δ (i+1) ≫ b) ≫ d i = (δ (i+1) ≫ δ i) ≫ a = 0. Mathlib ShortComplex.Exact.liftFromProjective for hex i gives the next map c with c ≫ d (i+1) = δ (i+1) ≫ b.

Apply dependent Nat.rec to the sigma type of adjacent pairs, starting with (a₀,a₁), and sending (a,b) to (b,c). Let α i be the first map of the pair at i. The recursion equation identifies α (i+1) with the second map at i, so its recorded compatibility proves the desired equation; α 0 = a₀ is definitional.

lean.statement: theorem free_complex_extend_family (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (N : ModuleCat R) (N' : ℕ → ModuleCat R) (d : ∀ i : ℕ, N' (i + 1) ⟶ N' i) (η : N' 0 ⟶ N) (hd0 : d 0 ≫ η = 0) (hd : ∀ i : ℕ, d (i + 1) ≫ d i = 0) (hex0 : (ShortComplex.mk (d 0) η hd0).Exact) (hex : ∀ i : ℕ, (ShortComplex.mk (d (i + 1)) (d i) (hd i)).Exact) (F : ℕ → ModuleCat R) (δ : ∀ i : ℕ, F (i + 1) ⟶ F i) (hδ : ∀ i : ℕ, δ (i + 1) ≫ δ i = 0) (hfree : ∀ i : ℕ, Module.Free R (F i)) (a₀ : F 0 ⟶ N' 0) (ha₀ : δ 0 ≫ a₀ ≫ η = 0) : ∃ α : ∀ i : ℕ, F i ⟶ N' i, α 0 = a₀ ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, α (i + 1) ≫ d i = δ i ≫ α i)

old_proof.text: Starting from a₀, each obstruction lands in the next kernel by the two zero-composite identities; exactness makes the differential surjective onto that kernel and projectivity of the next free term gives a lift. Dependent recursion and choice assemble the compatible infinite family.
